record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For the Airy integral operator acting on L²(s,∞), can one determine the asymptotic behavior of its eigenfunctions as s→∞ and compute those eigenfunctions accurately for finite s?

evidence.quote: It is an open problem to analyze the behavior of the eigenfunctions u˜j(s) as s → ∞, and to compute their behavior for finite s.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each real number $s$, let $K_s$ denote the Airy integral operator acting on $L^2((s,\infty))$, defined by
$$(K_s f)(x) = \int_s^\infty K(x,y)\, f(y)\, dy, \qquad x > s,$$
with kernel
$$K(x,y) = \frac{\operatorname{Ai}(x)\operatorname{Ai}'(y) - \operatorname{Ai}'(x)\operatorname{Ai}(y)}{x-y},$$
where $\operatorname{Ai}$ is the Airy function. The operator $K_s$ is trace class, self-adjoint, and positive, with a discrete spectrum $1 > \lambda_1(s) > \lambda_2(s) > \cdots > 0$ and a corresponding orthonormal sequence of eigenfunctions $\{\tilde u_j(\cdot\,;s)\}_{j\ge 1} \subset L^2((s,\infty))$ satisfying
$$\int_s^\infty K(x,y)\, \tilde u_j(y;s)\, dy = \lambda_j(s)\, \tilde u_j(x;s).$$

(a) Determine the asymptotic behavior of the eigenfunctions $\tilde u_j(\cdot\,;s)$ as $s \to \infty$ (for each fixed $j$, and uniformly or with explicit error terms where appropriate).

(b) Provide a method to compute the eigenfunctions $\tilde u_j(\cdot\,;s)$ accurately for finite values of $s$.
artifact.status_search_result: The computational/finite-$s$ part has been substantially addressed: Bornemann (2021, "On the Evaluation of the Eigendecomposition of the Airy Integral Operator", arXiv:2104.12958) gives a numerical algorithm exploiting a commuting differential operator, computing eigenvalues and eigenfunctions (as scaled-Laguerre expansions) to full relative precision. The analytic asymptotic behavior of the eigenfunctions as $s\to\infty$ does not appear to have a complete published rigorous treatment; thus the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On the Evaluation of the Eigendecomposition of the Airy Integral Operator
status_evidence.snippet: Efficient algorithm computing the eigendecomposition of the Airy integral operator to full relative precision via a commuting differential operator; eigenfunctions expanded in scaled Laguerre functions.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses accurate computation of the Airy operator eigenfunctions for finite s.

status_evidence.title: On the evaluation of the eigendecomposition of the Airy integral operator - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Published version describing characterization of eigenfunctions and a numerical method.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the finite-s computational part has been resolved in published form.
